garv224.summary: Cipher telegrams between the Ministry of War in Bogotá and Gen. Amadeo Rodríguez Vergara, civil and military chief of the Amazonas, at Puerto Asís, 9-27 September 1932, the first weeks after the Peruvian seizure of Leticia (1 Sept 1932): ammunition from Bofors, the gunboats Cartagena, Santa Marta and Barranquilla, the state of the troops (499 men, corrected to 599), the move to Caucayá, the passage of Güepí, the Napo and the risk of a conflict with Ecuador, Peruvian reinforcements to Loreto, censorship of soldiers' letters.
garv224.en:
Same marks as the reading: {x} probable, [...] unresolved. "Gunboat" = cañonero.

urgent to order from the Bofors firm a thousand armour-piercing shells, a thousand shrapnel, a thousand shells for the gunboats' artillery pieces; today both have only two hundred and ninety shrapnel and two hundred and ninety-six shells; I judge it advisable to transfer the gunboat Barranquilla to form part of the Amazon flotilla, since the Peruvians have five war launches and numerous merchant vessels that can easily be armed for war; the Barranquilla could be taken by her crew under your orders, buying fuel at Curaçao; if the Ministry decides to send the gunboat Barranquilla, request transport of ammunition urgently, and the artillery pieces are at Cartagena; the gunboats' ammunition must be placed

Manaos: the steamer Nariño {sailed} [for] {Tocantins}, radio receiver-transmitter, wavelength [...]

system: Seven day-of-week simple-substitution alphabets (Sección I key, 31 Jan 1931), vowels to vowels; day and D/R in clear at the head.
